sim_verification.own_adversarial_strategy: Blindly choose a random diagnosis and evidence subset across two attempts; fresh execution produced 3.06%. Select-all remained 0%, and fixed displayed positions with two diagnosis slots produced 3.26%, consistent with chance. A clinically informed {exam,lab,xray} submission wins. {lab,xray,spo2} is reasonably rejected because the player is asked to select decisive differential evidence: SpO2 establishes severity/hypoxemia but does not distinguish these four candidates. Normal BP is likewise non-discriminating. Requiring lab+xray while making talk/exam optional is a defensible line for this simplified case.
sim_verification.notes: Executed the current simulation logic from stdin because the read-only workspace prevented its final writeFileSync. All four legitimate variants returned 100%; exactly four of 252 joint diagnosis/evidence combinations won. Executable logic is correct, although its historical comments contain stale exact-set/1-in-63 statements.
